title: L6 Capstone: Your Own Standard Library
story: You've built validators, math tools, and string utilities. Now combine them all into YOUR personal standard library - three modules, each with interfaces, types, and functions. These are tools you'll carry into every future program. You've built your own standard library!
why: This capstone synthesizes modules, interfaces, generics, and contracts into a personal toolkit that demonstrates mastery of L6 engineering concepts.
analogy: A master craftsman builds their own tool chest - custom-fitted wrenches, sharpened chisels, calibrated measuring tools. Your standard library is that tool chest. You made it. You know every piece. It fits your hands perfectly.
try_it: Expand each module with 2-3 more functions of your choosing. Add contracts to the math module functions. Create a new program that imports your library and solves a real problem - like a prime factorization tool or a text analyzer.
tips: Name your modules clearly: my_math, my_string, my_collections
Each module should have a single responsibility
This library is yours forever - invest in making it clean and useful
common_mistakes: Putting everything in one giant module - separate concerns
Making everything private - mark your API functions as pub
Not testing each module independently before combining them
